newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mine blast kills two on Red Cross bus in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mine blast kills two on Red Cross bus in Zaire.

text.p: An anti-personnel mine killed two people and wounded up to 33 on a Red Cross bus in eastern Zaire's refugee zone on Saturday, senior Red Cross officials said. All the dead were Zairean.

Vicent Nicod, International Committee of the Red Cross delegate in Kinshasa, said the bus went over the mine as it was transporting a medical team from the town of Goma to Kimbumba camp, one of several in the region housing Rwandan refugees.
Estimates of the number of wounded ranged from 18 to 33.
"We have no idea who was behind this. It could be an act of revenge," Nicod said.
Lino Bordin, his counterpart in Goma, said the incident happened near the airport and followed a period of relative calm in the volatile region.
Over a million Hutus fled to Zaire in 1994 fearing revenge attacks after Hutu hardliners killed hundreds of thousands of minority Tutsis and Tutsi-led rebels won power.
